entries.name: Trout and char daily quota
entries.regs_verbatim: Zone B Daily Quotas. Trout/char: 5, but not more than 1 over 50 cm, 2 from streams, 2 lake trout, 1 bull trout. NOTE: Bull trout may only be retained from Oct 16-Aug 14. These fish may only be from the Liard River watershed (or other specified waters) and only 30-50 cm in length. And you must release: Rainbow trout of any size from streams, May 1-June 15, Lake trout under 30 cm, Lake trout of any size, Sept 15-Oct 31, Bull trout from the Liard River watershed Aug 15-Oct 15, and from the Peace River watershed all year.

rules.verbatim: Trout/char: 5
1 over 50 cm
2 from streams
2 lake trout
NOTE: Bull trout may only be retained from Oct 16-Aug 14. These fish may only be from the Liard River watershed (or other specified waters) and only 30-50 cm in length.
rules.extent_text: Liard River watershed, or other specified waters
rules.review_reason: Bound to the Liard watershed, where the chapter says bull trout may be retained. The operative quota is stated water-specifically by `r7:liard_river_watershed…@7-53` ('daily and possession quotas = 1 (none under 30 cm or over 50 cm), Oct 16-Aug 14'), which outranks this. Kept because it is the REGION's statement that bull trout may be kept nowhere else in Zone B — '(or other specified waters)' is the carve-out and it is not enumerated.

rules.verbatim: Rainbow trout of any size from streams, May 1-June 15
Lake trout under 30 cm
Lake trout of any size, Sept 15-Oct 31
Bull trout from the Liard River watershed Aug 15-Oct 15, and from the Peace River watershed all year
rules.review_reason: The PEACE half of a sentence naming two watersheds with different windows. The verbatim keeps the whole sentence so the reader can see what it is a half OF; the extent and the absent window are what make this rule the Peace one. The Liard half is r9b.

rules.verbatim: Bull trout from the Liard River watershed Aug 15-Oct 15, and from the Peace River watershed all year
rules.review_reason: The LIARD half, with its own window. `r7:liard_river_watershed…@7-53` states it water-specifically and outranks this, but the zone rule is what renders where the water rule does not reach.

entries.name: Peace River navigation
entries.regs_verbatim: PEACE RIVER The Peace River is no longer navigable past the Site C construction site. Avoid boat travel between 2 km upstream of the dam site and the downstream construction bridge.

rules.verbatim: PEACE RIVER The Peace River is no longer navigable past the Site C construction site. Avoid boat travel between 2 km upstream of the dam site and the downstream construction bridge.
rules.extent_text: Peace River at the Site C site
rules.review_reason: BOUND — named water. Water-scoped safety notice. RECOVERED — absent from the corpus.

entries.name: Thin ice — Inga and Sundance
entries.regs_verbatim: THIN ICE AND OPEN WATER Due to aeration projects, dangerous thin ice and open water may exist on Inga and Sundance lakes. It is prohibited to enter within the fenced area surrounding the aerator.

rules.verbatim: Due to aeration projects, dangerous thin ice and open water may exist on Inga and Sundance lakes.
It is prohibited to enter within the fenced area surrounding the aerator.
rules.extent_text: the fenced area surrounding the aerator
rules.review_reason: A PROHIBITION ON ENTERING a fenced area, not an angling closure — as access_permission it rendered 'Angling prohibited', which would tell a reader the lake is closed to fishing when it is not. Typed hazard until an access type exists that can say 'do not enter' without implying a fishing ban. Sundance Lake is not in the registry index.

entries.name: Ice fishing huts
entries.scope_note: SPLIT: one sentence carried a 'should' and an offence. Rendering both as law is the mirror of rendering law as advice.
entries.regs_verbatim: ICE FISHING HUTS Ice fishing huts should have the owner's contact information displayed in a prominent location when left unoccupied.
